title: Republic of Hawai'i
capsule: The Republic of Hawaiʻi (Lepupalika ʻo Hawaiʻi) was a one-party oligarchic state that came into existence on 4 July 1894, replacing the Provisional Government formed after the January 1893 overthrow of Queen Liliʻuokalani. Its sole president was Sanford B. Dole, who presided over a constitutional order that disenfranchised Asian residents and frustrated the queen's repeated appeals for restoration. A royalist counter-coup in January 1895 led by Robert Wilcox was suppressed; Liliʻuokalani was arrested, tried, and later pardoned. The republic ended on 12 August 1898 when the Newlands Resolution, passed during the Spanish-American War, formally annexed Hawaiʻi to the United States as a territory.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Political and constitutional history is thoroughly documented in US government and Hawaiian archival sources; the de facto territorial extent (the archipelago) is unambiguous.
